headline: High Desert Canyons and Scenic Byway Access
reservation: Permits for backcountry hiking and camping are managed by the BLM; some areas require in-person registration at visitor centers. There is no central entry fee for the monument, but specific sites like Lower Calf Creek Falls have day-use fees. Check the BLM site for current fire and road restrictions.

days.title: Sandstone Landmarks and Canyons

stops.name: Lower Calf Creek Falls
stops.detail: A six-mile round-trip hike through a deep canyon ending at a 126-foot perennial waterfall.

stops.name: The Hogback
stops.detail: Drive this narrow ridge on Scenic Byway 12 for dramatic drops and views of the slickrock wilderness.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; conditions vary on winding canyon roads
days.note: Parking at Calf Creek is extremely limited; have an alternate plan ready.

days.title: Boulder Plateau and Ancestral History

stops.name: Anasazi State Park Museum
stops.detail: Explore an ancient Indigenous archaeological site and museum in the shadow of Boulder Mountain.

stops.name: Long Canyon (Burr Trail)
stops.detail: Drive the paved portion of the Burr Trail to see towering red wingate sandstone walls.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for the scenic loop; conditions vary
days.note: The Burr Trail becomes unpaved and steep past Long Canyon; check vehicle suitability.

days.title: Hole-in-the-Rock Formations

stops.name: Devils Garden
stops.detail: Walk among unique hoodoos and arches located just off the unpaved main corridor.

stops.name: Escalante Interagency Visitor Center
stops.detail: Consult rangers for updated road conditions before attempting any remote backcountry routes.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours; unpaved roads require slow speeds and high clearance
days.note: Hole-in-the-Rock Road can become impassable for all vehicles after rain.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Lower Calf Creek Falls lot often fills early; do not park on the highway shoulder. Devils Garden has a designated lot, but unpaved road conditions dictate access.

intel.title: Remote Desert Communications
intel.text: Cell service is largely unavailable outside the towns of Escalante and Boulder. Satellite messengers or offline maps are essential for all backcountry travel.

intel.title: Distance Between Services
intel.text: Fuel up in Escalante or Boulder; there are no services within the monument boundaries. Some stations have limited hours in the off-season.

intel.title: Flash Flood Safety
intel.text: Always check the forecast for regional rain; canyons can flood from storms many miles away. Sandstone hiking is best done in the cooler morning hours.

intel.title: Unpaved Road Hazards
intel.text: Monument roads like Hole-in-the-Rock are washboarded and clay-based. Rain turns these surfaces into slick mud that can strand even 4WD vehicles.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at PGA or a major hub like LAS. Stock up on water and desert-grade supplies in Page or Kanab before heading to the more remote Escalante base.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance 4WD is strongly recommended for unpaved monument roads. Check rental agreements for prohibitions against driving on unmaintained dirt surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: Kiva Coffeehouse Overlook offers a vast view of the Escalante River canyon, especially striking as shadows lengthen in autumn.
